NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for
  viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday following the
  meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 941 4931 5377, Meeting Password: 650005. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 941 4931 5377, Meeting Password: 650005
  Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
  following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand"
  option at the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which
  item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 28, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development and Public Works Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT "RECYCLING HERO" DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR OF
  FREE WASTE RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL REFUSE SERVICE – SECOND
  QUARTER 2020

Assistant City Manager Davis reported that Waste Management’s representative was
unable to attend the meeting and that the drawing would be postponed to a future
meeting. She also reported on behalf of Waste Management that solid waste collection
services have not been impacted, however the processing of recyclables and green waste
has changed due to COVID-19. Residents are encouraged to continue to separate their
trash, recyclables and green waste materials.

5.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CAL WATER UPDATE ON PALOS VERDES PIPELINE PROJECT

Karina Winje of Cal Water provided an update on the Palos Verdes Pipeline project.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZUCKERMAN TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 6A-F AS
  FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 28, 2020
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 14, 2020

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – MARCH 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 62643 THROUGH 62704 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $336,775.29 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040120 THROUGH
  040320 IN THE AMOUNT OF $103,195.60 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $439,970.89 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF MARCH 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF MARCH 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF APRIL 20, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2453 FOR APPROVAL OF THE CDBG-CV CARES
  ACT ADDITIONAL FUNDING TO ITS COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK
  GRANT (CDBG) PROGRAM AND BUDGET

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) receive any
  public testimony; 3) close the Public Hearing; 4) waive further reading; and 5)
  adopt Resolution No. 2453 approving the CDBG-CV CARES Act additional funding
  to its Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program and budget.

  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ called for public testimony. Public comment
  was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live Zoom
  Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media
  platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 28, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN,

  APPROVED RESOLUTION NO. 2453, APPROVING THE CDBG-CV
  CARES ACT ADDITIONAL FUNDING TO ITS COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG) PROGRAM AND BUDGET.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PROJECT LIST FOR SB 1 FUND ELIGIBILITY (RESOLUTION No. 2452)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2452, adopting a
  list of projects for Fiscal Year 2020-21 funded by SB 1, the Road Repair and
  Accountability Act of 2017.

  Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report
  (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF was pleased to see the portion of Palos Verdes Drive
  East to the City’s eastern limit included.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN confirmed that the Highridge Road section would
  include both sides of the road, and that project selections were based on the
  recommendations of the most recent Pavement Management System report.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED RESOLUTION NO. 2452, ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS
  FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-21 FUNDED BY SB 1, THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  REQUEST TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE 2020 STREET RESURFACING PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff to solicit bids for the FY 20-21
  Street Resurfacing Project.

  Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report
  (as per the agenda material).

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR THE FY 20-21 STREET
  RESURFACING PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 28, 2020
 C.  ORDINANCE NO. 730 AMENDING AND RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE
  CHAPTER 8.20 (INTEGRATED WASTE MANAGEMENT)

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) receive any public testimony; and 2)
  introduce Ordinance No. 730 on first reading.

  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis and City Attorney Don Davis provided a staff
  report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL inquired about the abbreviated language in the
  edible food recovery section, in which City Attorney Davis directed her to page 12
  of the proposed ordinance where edible food is incorporated by reference to
  comply with the California Code of Regulations.

  City Attorney Davis explained that this ordinance was drafted with the City’s Waste
  Management franchise in mind, and that the franchise agreement was made to be
  consistent with State Law, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL’S
  question. Assistant City Manager Davis further outlined the City’s plan to meet new
  requirements under SB 1383, noting that further amendments can be made if
  necessary.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted that while on the subcommittee for the
  Waste Management franchise agreement, the intention was to create flexibility in
  the agreement for current and new legislation, and that he is comfortable with the
  state of the current agreement.

  Assistant City Manager Davis clarified that food waste will not need to be
  separated from yard waste, and should go in the yard waste bin, in response to
  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCED ON FIRST READING ORDINANCE NO. 730, AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES, AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 8.20 OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO
  INTEGRATED WASTE MANAGEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

** ADJOURNED TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION CORPORATION MEETING **

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
ZERUNYAN, THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE
FOUNDATION CORPORATION MEETING.

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

D.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF APRIL
  20, 2020 - INSTALLATION LOCATION OF ARMENIAN GENOCIDE MEMORIAL

  Recommendation: That the Pepper Tree Foundation Board of Directors approve the
  proposed location for installation of the Armenian Genocide Memorial.

  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 28, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN displayed an image of the bronze plaque. He
  explained that fundraising is on hold currently due to the pandemic, and that he
  hopes the memorial will be placed and complete by the end of the year. He also
  noted that the Centennial plaque moving to the right of its current location will be
  more prominent than in its current location.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL asked for clarification on the size of the rock, art
  piece and plaque all in the relation to the wall it is being placed in front of, wanting
  to ensure they are in proportion with eachother. COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN
  explained that the total memorial size would be shorter than the wall itself and in
  proportion.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF stated that this memorial was a fitting way for the
  Council to convey its appreciation to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN upon his
  announcement of his retirement, since this is an issue he has been passionate
  about for as long as she’s known him, and hopes residents share in his
  enthusiasm.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN feels this will be a very nice addition to the
  grounds of City Hall. He inquired about the potential of future requests
  similar memorials and what the City’s process would be. City Manager
  Grammer explained that each request would be subject to the City’s “City
  Property and Facility Naming Policy and/or Recognition Plaque” guidelines
  and would be considered by both the Park & Activities Commission and the
  City Council for approval.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL stated that this memorial is distinguished
  from other memorials through COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN and his long
  dedication to both the City, the Armenian Genocide and all genocides throughout
  history.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ echoed the sentiments of COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN explained the reasoning behind selecting
  the image of the woman and child for the memorial.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed the rock would be a total of 6 feet, and
  that a portion would be stabilizing the rock underground.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website,
  and during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s
  website and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO
  TEM ZUCKERMAN TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL
  CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED THE PROPOSED LOCATION FOR INSTALLATION OF THE
  ARMENIAN GENOCIDE MEMORIAL.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  ABSTAIN:  Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN,
THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURN THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION
CORPORATION MEETING AND RECONVENE THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

** RECONVENED CITY COUNCIL MEETING **

E.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF APRIL
  20, 2020 - GRANT APPLICATION FOR MONTECILLO ENTRYWAY

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 28, 2020
   Recommendation: That the City Council approve $2,500 of the Street Entryway
  Beautification Program funds to the Montecillo HOA.

  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL commented that the sign was attractive, and
  confirmed it would be a white sign with green lettering.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms.

  Ed Mohr, Secretary of the Montecillo HOA commented on the proposed sign.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked the members of the HOA for their time and
  effort on designing and creating the sign, especially the Board Members and City
  staff.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED $2,500 OF THE STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION
  PROGRAM FUNDS TO THE MONTECILLO HOA.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

F.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION – CITY EVENTS UPDATE

  Recommendation: Receive and File.

  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho provided a staff report (as per
  the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL asked for the Council’s input regarding
  rescheduling the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride. Assistant City Manager Davis explained
  that the Boy Scouts’ schedule does not allow for them to participate if the event is
  rescheduled for later in the year, therefore other options are being considered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF inquired about the possibility of combining the Mayor’s
  Breakfast Ride with the City Celebration.

  Assistant City Manager Davis explained that physical distancing is possible with
  the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride event, and that this would be a wonderful first event
  once the City begins to open back up.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed that this event is near and dear to her heart, and
  hopes there will still be excitement surrounding the event with the postponement.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN inquired about potentially considering
  combining the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride with a July 4th Celebration.

  Assistant City Manager Davis stated that this recommendation would be shared
  with the Equestrian Committee at their May 11, 2020 Special Meeting. She also
  explained that only the first Movie Night in June has been canceled thus far.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
APRIL 28, 2020
 10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE NON-RESIDENTIAL DEFAULT CHANGE

  Recommendation: Non-residential accounts in Rolling Hills Estates are currently
  defaulted in the most cost effective rate tier for electrical service, saving them 1%-
  2% on their bill, compared to the costs they would incur, if they opted-out of CPA and
  returned to SCE. Given the current economic challenges non-residential accounts
  are facing due to the COVID-19 pandemic, staff recommends that the City Council
  take no action at this time.

  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda
  material).

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN read a letter encouraging the Council to
  consider the change from Lean to Clean Power, despite being in the midst of the
  COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the magnitude of the dangers and health
  impacts caused by air pollution each and every year. He also emphasized the
  minimal difference in cost between Lean and Clean Power, yet the significant
  difference in reduction of pollution.

  Planning Manager Naughton confirmed that switching to the Clean Power rate tier
  would still offer a break-even to 1% savings to Non-Residential accounts, in
  response to MAYOR SCHMITZ.

  Discussion ensued regarding the average savings to customers in the two tiers
  and when these changes would take place if approved.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL discussed the various letters she has received in
  favor of the change in spite of the COVID-19 pandemic.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN discussed the optics of this change if the
  Council chooses to approve the change during the pandemic. He highlighted that
  some businesses will never be able to reopen, and asked the Council to be
  empathetic to this. He stated that he supports this change so long as the price
  change is minimal to none for City businesses.

  Discussion ensued regarding the average savings, and potential of changing rates
  due to the cost of energy.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN reminded the Council that all accounts have the
  option to switch up or down or opt out at will, and that communication regarding
  the change will be extremely important.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ confirmed if the change is made, it would apply through 2021,
  and the next opportunity to change again would be in 2022.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that CPA pays for two mailers to communicate
  the change to all customers affected. MAYOR SCHMITZ stressed the importance
  of communication within these mailers to illustrate the three options available to
  customers.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms.

  Michelle Ellison spoke in favor of changing to 100% Clean Power.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZUCKERMAN TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:
